text.p: Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Friday its production of gold rose about 29 percent to 449,811 ounces in calendar 1996 from 1995.
December quarter production totalled 132,555 ounces, a 13.1 percent rise over the corresponding period a year earlier.
The company's flagship Plutonic gold mine in Western Australia produced 67,751 ounces in the latest quarter, a 44 percent rise on the precious three months, the company said.
Cash operating costs over the same period improved to A$326 an ounce from A$352, to average A$373 for all of 1996.

"Further cost reductions are expected in 1997. Operating costs at some of the group's smaller mines have been unacceptably high but operating improvements are expected to reduce costs to acceptable levels in 1997," the company said.
The 66.7 percent owned Peak Hill Gold Mine produced 15,816 ounces (Plutonic's share 10,545) at a cash operating cost of A$278 per ounce (September A$245).
The Mount Morgans deposit, 80 percent owned by Plutonic, yielded 28,630 ounces (Plutonic's share 22,903) at a cash operating cost of A$504 per ounce.

Darlot Gold Mine produced 15,659 ounces at a cash operating cost of A$477 per ounce. The wholly-owned Lawler/Bellevue operation performed poorly with high cost production of an aggregate 15,697 ounces as development of the new Henderson Pit at Bellevue was slower than anticipated, the company said.
